back: The product of the ion concentrations in a saturated solution of a sparingly soluble salt, each raised to the power of its coefficient, at a given temperature.
AB: Ksp = s². AB₂ or A₂B: Ksp = 4s³. AB₃: Ksp = 27s⁴.
Calculate the ionic product after mixing (halve for equal volumes); precipitate if it exceeds Ksp.
A sparingly soluble salt is less soluble in a solution already containing one of its ions.
s = Ksp ÷ [common ion], assuming the common ion comes only from the added salt.
AgCl: mol² dm⁻⁶. PbI₂, Ag₂CrO₄, Ca(OH)₂: mol³ dm⁻⁹.
Only temperature. A common ion lowers the solubility, not Ksp.
Compare Ksp values directly only for salts of the same formula type; otherwise calculate s.
